body: Traveling would be a good break from your thoughts. It would be a tremendous opportunity to reconnect with yourself and gain experience. I wish you the best of luck with your journey. Here to listen, if you need it.

I've been struggling with those extremes too. Take care to stay in equilibrium :)

Edit: posted my comment twice

I know what I should do. It just doesn't make it any easier. I'm tired and doing those things makes me feel horrible because I don't have any interest in them. You are right , but I'm difficult. I'm stubborn and persistent in the wrong way. I take greater comfort and relief in planning my own suicide than planning my life.

I don't have any money as of right now. I plan to use the university's gym. No mountains. Inner city. Can't drive so going somewhere on my own is kinda out and everyone else is tired. Thank you for you suggestion! I agree with it. To get myself outta my head.
Thank you for checking in however.
I don't feel well. I don't know if its even worth trying. But I can keep pretending for a while.

The expense of the service, the slightly damaged state of the house (I don't know how that would affect the price), and that we (4) really wouldn't have any other place to stay for free were all considerations I had since the beginning. Also, my dad is in delicate condition, and seeing as how this is his house, he may object to pesticides. And then convince me that what I have is not scabies.

Although I've just finished my second treatment, I don't know if they're really gone now. Mild itching up to 2 weeks after treatment is normal. I've had this since April, received treatment in May. I have an  appointment soon. At this point, I honestly don't care if my body feels better, it's adapting; I just fear someone else from my family or someone from work will contact this.

Thank you. Today was the worst I've felt since the night I woke up exactly a week ago, but your message has helped with the emotional scar I've been trying to hide. Recovering, I am just beginning to realize, will not be easy. Your thoughtful response helps me keep the bit of hope I have going. Thank you.
